import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.48

by V. N. Remeslennikov

Suppose that $G$ and $H$ are finitely generated residually finite groups having the same set
of finite homomorphic images. Are $G$ and $H$ isomorphic if one of them is a free (free
soluble) group?

The problem consists of two parallel questions: one where the distinguished group is free,
and one where it is free soluble, i.e. of the form $F/F^{(d)}$ for a free group $F$ and
some $d$ (a free group in the variety of soluble groups of derived length at most $d$).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 5.48.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.48»

universe u

/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if for every $g \neq 1$ in $G$ there is a homomorphism
from $G$ to a finite group that does not send $g$ to $1$. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ (Q : Type u) (_ : Group Q) (_ : Finite Q) (φ : G →* Q), φ g ≠ 1

/-- Two groups $G$ and $H$ have the *same set of finite homomorphic images* if every finite
group is a homomorphic image (the image of a surjective homomorphism) of $G$ exactly when it is
a homomorphic image of $H$. This property is invariant under isomorphism of the finite group,
so it says that the sets of finite quotients of $G$ and of $H$, taken up to isomorphism,
coincide. -/
def HasSameFiniteQuotients (G H : Type*) [Group G] [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∀ (Q : Type) [Group Q] [Finite Q],
    (∃ φ : G →* Q, Function.Surjective φ) ↔ ∃ ψ : H →* Q, Function.Surjective ψ

attribute [local instance] derivedSeries_normal

/-- A group $G$ is *free soluble* if it is isomorphic to $F/F^{(d)}$ for some free group $F$
and some $d \geq 0$, where $F^{(d)}$ is the $d$-th term of the derived series of $F$. Equivalently,
$G$ is a free group in the variety of soluble groups of derived length at most $d$. -/
def IsFreeSolvable (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι : Type u) (d : ℕ), Nonempty (G ≃* FreeGroup ι ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup ι) d)

/-- Every finite group is residually finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsResiduallyFinite.of_finite (G : Type u) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun _ hg => ⟨G, inferInstance, inferInstance, MonoidHom.id G, hg⟩

/-- A group has the same finite homomorphic images as itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem HasSameFiniteQuotients.refl (G : Type*) [Group G] : HasSameFiniteQuotients G G :=
  fun _ _ _ => Iff.rfl

/-- The quotient $F/F^{(d)}$ of a free group by a term of its derived series is free soluble. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFreeSolvable_freeGroup_quotient_derivedSeries (ι : Type u) (d : ℕ) :
    IsFreeSolvable (FreeGroup ι ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup ι) d) :=
  ⟨ι, d, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- Free soluble groups are soluble. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFreeSolvable.isSolvable {G : Type u} [Group G] (hG : IsFreeSolvable G) :
    IsSolvable G := by
  obtain ⟨ι, d, ⟨e⟩⟩ := hG
  have hd : derivedSeries (FreeGroup ι ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup ι) d) d = ⊥ := by
    rw [← map_derivedSeries_eq (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective _), eq_bot_iff]
    exact Subgroup.map_le_iff_le_comap.2 fun x hx => by
      simpa [Subgroup.mem_comap, QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff] using hx
  haveI : IsSolvable (FreeGroup ι ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup ι) d) := ⟨⟨d, hd⟩⟩
  exact solvable_of_solvable_injective (f := e.toMonoidHom) e.injective

/--
Suppose that $G$ and $H$ are finitely generated residually finite groups having the same set
of finite homomorphic images. Are $G$ and $H$ isomorphic if one of them is a free group?

Since the hypotheses are symmetric in $G$ and $H$, we may assume that $G$ is the free group.
A finitely generated free group has finite rank (the trivial group, of rank $0$, is allowed)
and is residually finite, so the hypothesis of residual finiteness on $G$ is automatic, but it
is kept to match the statement.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.48».parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H] [Group.FG G] [Group.FG H],
      IsResiduallyFinite G → IsResiduallyFinite H → HasSameFiniteQuotients G H →
      IsFreeGroup G → Nonempty (G ≃* H) := by
  sorry

/--
Suppose that $G$ and $H$ are finitely generated residually finite groups having the same set
of finite homomorphic images. Are $G$ and $H$ isomorphic if one of them is a free soluble
group?

Since the hypotheses are symmetric in $G$ and $H$, we may assume that $G$ is the free soluble
group, i.e. $G \cong F/F^{(d)}$ for some free group $F$ and some $d \geq 0$; as $G$ is finitely
generated, $F$ can be taken of finite rank. Free soluble groups are residually finite
(Gruenberg), so the hypothesis of residual finiteness on $G$ is automatic, but it is kept to
match the statement.
-/

    ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H] [Group.FG G] [Group.FG H],
      IsResiduallyFinite G → IsResiduallyFinite H → HasSameFiniteQuotients G H →
      IsFreeSolvable G → Nonempty (G ≃* H) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.48»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.48

by V. N. Remeslennikov

Suppose that $G$ and $H$ are finitely generated residually finite groups having the same set
of finite homomorphic images. Are $G$ and $H$ isomorphic if one of them is a free
(free soluble) group?

Two finitely generated groups have the same set of finite homomorphic images (up to
isomorphism) if and only if their profinite completions are isomorphic, so the free case asks
whether finitely generated free groups are *profinitely rigid* among finitely generated
residually finite groups. The parenthetical question asks the same with "free" replaced by
"free soluble", i.e. free in the variety of soluble groups of derived length at most $d$
for some $d$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

universe u

namespace Kourovka.«5.48»

/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if every non-identity element of $G$ lies outside
some normal subgroup of finite index; equivalently, every non-identity element has a
non-identity image in some finite homomorphic image of $G$. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- Two groups $G$ and $H$ have the *same set of finite homomorphic images* if every finite
group is a homomorphic image (surjective image) of $G$ if and only if it is a homomorphic
image of $H$. Since every finite group is isomorphic to one in `Type`, quantifying over
finite groups `Q : Type` captures "the same finite quotients up to isomorphism". -/
def HasSameFiniteQuotients (G H : Type*) [Group G] [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∀ (Q : Type) [Group Q] [Finite Q],
    (∃ φ : G →* Q, Function.Surjective φ) ↔ (∃ ψ : H →* Q, Function.Surjective ψ)

/-- A group $G$ is *free soluble* if it is isomorphic to $F / F^{(d)}$ for some free group
$F$ and some $d \in \mathbb{N}$, where $F^{(d)}$ is the $d$-th term of the derived series
of $F$; that is, $G$ is free in the variety of soluble groups of derived length at most $d$. -/
def IsFreeSolvable (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (α : Type u) (d : ℕ), Nonempty (G ≃* FreeGroup α ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup α) d)

/-- Finite groups are residually finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsResiduallyFinite.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun g hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa [Subgroup.mem_bot] using hg⟩

/-- Every group has the same finite homomorphic images as itself. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem HasSameFiniteQuotients.refl (G : Type*) [Group G] : HasSameFiniteQuotients G G :=
  fun _ _ _ => Iff.rfl

/-- Having the same finite homomorphic images is a symmetric relation. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem HasSameFiniteQuotients.symm {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H]
    (h : HasSameFiniteQuotients G H) : HasSameFiniteQuotients H G :=
  fun Q _ _ => (h Q).symm

/-- The quotient $F / F^{(d)}$ of a free group $F$ by a term of its derived series is free
soluble. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFreeSolvable_freeGroup_quotient_derivedSeries (α : Type u) (d : ℕ) :
    IsFreeSolvable (FreeGroup α ⧸ derivedSeries (FreeGroup α) d) :=
  ⟨α, d, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- A free soluble group is soluble. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFreeSolvable.isSolvable {G : Type u} [Group G] (h : IsFreeSolvable G) :
    IsSolvable G := by
  obtain ⟨α, d, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  let π : FreeGroup α →* G :=
    e.symm.toMonoidHom.comp (QuotientGroup.mk' (derivedSeries (FreeGroup α) d))
  have hπ : Function.Surjective π :=
    e.symm.surjective.comp (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective _)
  refine ⟨⟨d, ?_⟩⟩
  rw [← map_derivedSeries_eq hπ, Subgroup.map_eq_bot_iff]

  simpa [π, QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff] using hx
